Radar Cross Section (RCS) measurement data can be analyzed using ISAR images.
Backprojection uses the adjoint operator A† to estimate the scattering image.
Iterative smooth reweighted ℓ1-minimization promotes sparsity and cluster sparsity in ISAR images.
The forward model is Ax = y, where A is the forward operator and y is measured RCS amplitude.
The ℓ1-minimization problem is formulated as minimizing ||x||_1 subject to ||Ax - y||_2 ≤ κ.
The smoothing function D(Δr) = 1 - (Δr/d) for Δr < d is used to smooth the image in the iterative method.
The reweighting matrix W is defined as W = 1/(x_D + η) to avoid division by zero.
Four iterations of reweighted ℓ1-minimization are used in the algorithm.
Simulations used a frequency range of 13.5–16.5 GHz with 41 frequency steps.
Azimuth angle range was from -5.7° to 5.7° with 41 angle steps.
Grid spacing for simulations was 1 cm.
Two isotropic point scatterers separated by 0.15 m and 0.05 m were used in simulations.
Backprojection accurately extracts RCS for scatterers separated by more than 0.2 m.
Iterative smooth reweighted ℓ1-minimization can resolve scatterers closer than 0.2 m but with less accuracy.
Backprojection is more robust and accurate but limited by resolution.
Iterative smooth reweighted ℓ1-minimization improves resolution but may spread point clusters due to grid mismatch.
RCS is related to the squared magnitude of the complex scattering amplitude: σ[m²] = |y|².
Backprojection images are straightforward to implement and robust.
The iterative method uses element-wise multiplication of W and x in the ℓ1-norm minimization.
The parameter κ is set to 0.01 times the norm of y in simulations to control data misfit.
